- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.20) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent lows.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
